question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

You have exactly one hour to completes the exam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hour to complete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure here is noun + to + V1 (infinitive of purpose). After the marker "to" we must use the base form (V1) of the verb, never a finite form like "completes" or "completed".

◦ Correct: You have exactly one hour to complete the exam.

• "one hour" is a singular noun phrase telling us how much time is available; the infinitive "to complete" tells us what that hour is for.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "completes" (V5 / s-form) after "to" is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "hour to completed" wrongly puts the past participle (V3) after "to".

• Option 3 "hourly to complete" is wrong: "hourly" is an adjective/adverb meaning "every hour" (प्रति घंटा) and cannot follow "one".

NOTE

• Rule: to + V1 in a to-infinitive. e.g. "time to go", "work to finish", "a lot to learn".

• Do not confuse the infinitive "to" (to + V1) with the preposition "to" (to + V1-ing), as in "look forward to meeting you".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Ethnic Cleansing
option_1: Worshiping of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale
option_2: Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale
option_3: One who was previously unknown and is now prominent
option_4: A large number of people either falling ill or dying
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ethnic cleansing" means the mass killing or forced removal of the members of one ethnic or religious group from an area by another group. (जातीय सफाया / नस्ली संहार)

◦ Example: The war crimes tribunal described the massacres as an act of ethnic cleansing.

• The word "cleansing" is used ironically/euphemistically here — the perpetrators speak of "cleaning" an area of an unwanted community.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Worshiping ... on a massive scale" reverses the sense completely — there is nothing devotional about the term.

• Option 3 "One who was previously unknown and is now prominent" is the meaning of "an upstart" or "a dark horse".

• Option 4 "A large number of people either falling ill or dying" describes an "epidemic" or a "pestilence", not ethnic cleansing.

NOTE

• Related vocabulary often asked in SSC exams: genocide (नरसंहार — deliberate killing of a large group), exodus (पलायन — mass departure), pogrom (organised massacre), diaspora (प्रवासी समुदाय).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

They (are waiting) for the bus when the accident happened.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. were waiting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "when the accident happened" is in the simple past. The action of waiting was already in progress at that past moment, so the main clause needs the past continuous tense: "were waiting".

◦ Correct: They were waiting for the bus when the accident happened.

• Structure: Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing) + when + Simple Past — the longer background action is in the past continuous, the sudden/short action in the simple past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No correction required" keeps the present continuous "are waiting", which clashes with the past-tense verb "happened".

• Option 2 "have waited" (present perfect) and Option 4 "have been waiting" (present perfect continuous) both belong to present time and cannot be used with a definite past time clause.

NOTE

• Rule of tense harmony: in a complex sentence with a past-tense principal clause, the subordinate clause normally also takes a past form.

• Compare: "I was reading when the phone rang." / "While she was cooking, the lights went off."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

After the first defeats he had to ______ from France with the empress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Flee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flee" (verb) means to run away from danger, to escape. (भाग जाना / पलायन करना)

◦ Correct: After the first defeats he had to flee from France with the empress.

• After the modal-like structure "had to", we need a verb in the base form, and "flee" is the only verb among the options that fits the sense of escaping after a defeat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Fleet" is a noun meaning a group of ships/vehicles (बेड़ा); as an adjective it means "swift".

• Option 2 "Fling" means to throw something forcefully (फेंकना) — it does not suit "from France".

• Option 4 "Flea" is a noun meaning a small blood-sucking insect (पिस्सू) — a classic homophone trap.

NOTE

• Learn the forms: flee – fled – fled. e.g. "The thieves fled the scene."

• Frequently confused sets in SSC: flee/flea, fleet/flit, cite/site/sight, principal/principle.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Bite the bullet
option_4: Decide to do something that is difficult
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Decide to do something that is difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bite the bullet" means to force yourself to do something unpleasant or difficult, or to face a painful situation bravely. (कठिन परिस्थिति का साहस से सामना करना)

◦ Example: Fees were rising, so we had to bite the bullet and change schools.

• Origin: before anaesthetics, wounded soldiers were given a bullet to bite on during surgery so that they could bear the pain — hence "enduring something painful with courage".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To bring harm to someone" would be "to do someone a bad turn".

• Option 2 "To ruin oneself" is closer to "to dig one's own grave" / "to cut one's own throat".

• Option 3 "Peace talking" has no idiomatic connection with the phrase.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of endurance: "face the music" (परिणाम भुगतना), "take the bull by the horns" (कठिनाई का डटकर सामना करना), "grin and bear it", "stick it out".

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

Ruffin is seeking that (harmony) of humour in truth-telling amid despair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Discord.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harmony" means agreement, accord, a pleasing combination of parts. (सामंजस्य / मेल)

• "Discord" means disagreement, lack of harmony, conflict. (मतभेद / असामंजस्य) — the exact opposite.

◦ Antonym pair: harmony × discord.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Conformity" means compliance with rules or standards (अनुरूपता) — a synonym-side word, not an antonym.

• Option 3 "Sectional" means relating to a section or a particular group (अनुभागीय) — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Determination" means firmness of purpose (दृढ़ संकल्प) — unrelated.

NOTE

• Other antonyms of harmony: conflict, friction, strife, dissonance, disagreement.

• Synonyms of harmony: concord, accord, unison, rapport, congruity.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

I could not make out what / it is, for the wind was / rustling the corn-shocks.
option_1: I could not make out what
option_4: it is, for the wind was
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. it is, for the wind was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The principal clause is in the past tense ("I could not make out"). By the rule of sequence of tenses, the noun clause must also shift to the past: "what it was", not "what it is".

◦ Correct: I could not make out what it was, for the wind was rustling the corn-shocks.

• Notice that the very same segment already contains "the wind was" — proof that the narration is set in the past, so "is" is inconsistent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "I could not make out what" is correct — "make out" is a phrasal verb meaning "to see/understand with difficulty".

• Option 3 "rustling the corn-shocks." is correct as part of the past continuous "the wind was rustling".

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong since a clear tense error exists.

NOTE

• Sequence of tenses: past main verb → past subordinate verb (He said that he was ill).

• Exception: a universal truth keeps the present tense — "The teacher said that the earth is round."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Inclusive of private packs it is difficult to _______ more than an overall total of 60 drag and/or bloodhound packs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. envisage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Envisage" means to imagine, foresee or contemplate something as a possibility in the future. (कल्पना करना / परिकल्पना करना)

◦ Correct: ... it is difficult to envisage more than an overall total of 60 drag and/or bloodhound packs.

• The sentence is about estimating/imagining a maximum number, so "envisage" alone gives a sensible meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "haemorrhage" means heavy bleeding (रक्तस्राव) — medically unrelated.

• Option 2 "package" means to pack goods (पैकेट में बंद करना) — meaningless here.

• Option 4 "discourage" means to dishearten or dissuade (हतोत्साहित करना) — does not fit "more than a total of 60 packs".

NOTE

• Synonyms of envisage: envision, visualise, foresee, anticipate, contemplate.

• British spelling "haemorrhage" (American: hemorrhage) — note the silent -rrh- cluster, a favourite spelling question.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Humans are drawn to foods that is fatty, sweet, rich and complex.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. foods that is fatty,.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative pronoun "that" here refers back to the plural noun "foods". A relative pronoun takes the number and person of its antecedent, so the verb must be plural: "foods that are fatty".

◦ Correct: Humans are drawn to foods that are fatty, sweet, rich and complex.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Humans are drawn to" is correct — plural subject "Humans" with plural verb "are".

• Option 2 "sweet, rich and complex." is a correct list of adjectives.

• Option 1 "No error" is wrong because of the subject–verb disagreement noted above.

NOTE

• Rule: The verb after a relative pronoun (who/which/that) agrees with the antecedent.

◦ "He is one of the boys who play well." (antecedent = boys)

◦ "This is the only one of the books that is useful." (antecedent = one)

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Someone thinks Charles should _______ the British throne and come out here instead.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. abdicate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abdicate" means to give up or renounce a throne, high office or responsibility formally. (सिंहासन/पद त्यागना)

◦ Correct: Someone thinks Charles should abdicate the British throne and come out here instead.

• The object "the British throne" makes "abdicate" the only natural collocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "reciprocate" means to respond to an action with a similar one (प्रतिदान करना).

• Option 3 "decorticate" is a technical word meaning to remove the bark, husk or outer layer.

• Option 4 "authenticate" means to prove something genuine (प्रामाणिक सिद्ध करना).

NOTE

• Static link often used in exams: King Edward VIII of Britain abdicated in 1936; the noun form is "abdication".

• Word family: abdicate (verb) – abdication (noun); compare "adjudicate" (to judge) and "dedicate" (to devote).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

_________ in biotechnology and medicine have resulted in higher expectancy rate and lower mortality rate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Advancements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Advancements" means progress, improvements or developments. (प्रगति / उन्नति)

◦ Correct: Advancements in biotechnology and medicine have resulted in higher expectancy rate and lower mortality rate.

• Two clues confirm it: (i) the plural verb "have resulted" needs a plural subject, and (ii) only "progress" logically produces higher life expectancy and lower mortality.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Arrogate" is a verb meaning to claim something without justification (हथिया लेना) — a verb cannot be the subject here.

• Option 3 "Aversions" means strong dislikes (घृणा / विमुखता) — the opposite of a cause of progress.

• Option 4 "Saturation" is singular (संतृप्ति) and does not agree with "have resulted".

NOTE

• Useful collocations: advancements in science/technology/medicine; advances in research.

• Related terms: life expectancy (जीवन प्रत्याशा), mortality rate (मृत्यु दर), morbidity (रुग्णता).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Far, far at the top of them, / a shower of bright red sparks / had flared among the stars.
option_1: Far, far at the top of them,
option_3: a shower of bright red sparks
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Far, far at the top of them,.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes sparks flying high up in the sky over the people. The correct prepositional expression for this is "far, far above them", not "at the top of them".

◦ Correct: Far, far above them, a shower of bright red sparks had flared among the stars.

• "At the top of" is used with a thing that has a top — "at the top of the page / the hill / the stairs". It is not used with a pronoun standing for people to mean "overhead".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "a shower of bright red sparks" is correct — "a shower of" is a proper collective expression.

• Option 4 "had flared among the stars." is correct — past perfect "had flared", and "among" is right because the stars are more than two.

• Option 2 "No error" is therefore wrong.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place worth revising: above/over (ऊपर, without contact), on (contact), at the top of (fixed point of an object), among (more than two) vs between (two).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

Christian turned round and (strided off into) the blackness and I got into my car.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. strode off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stride" is an irregular verb: stride – strode – stridden. Its past tense is "strode", never the invented form "strided".

◦ Correct: Christian turned round and strode off into the blackness and I got into my car.

• "Stride off" means to walk away with long, decisive steps. (लंबे डग भरते हुए चल देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "strode of" and Option 3 "strided of" use the preposition "of" in place of the adverb particle "off" — a very common trap; "of" cannot form a phrasal verb here.

• Option 4 "No correction required" is wrong because "strided" is not an English word form.

NOTE

• Similar irregular verbs: ride – rode – ridden, write – wrote – written, drive – drove – driven, stride – strode – stridden.

• Remember: off = away/separated (adverb particle); of = belonging to (preposition).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A person who has money especially invested in business
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Capitalist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "capitalist" is a person who owns wealth or capital, especially money invested in a business or enterprise. (पूंजीपति)

◦ One-word substitution: "A person who has money especially invested in business" = Capitalist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Industrialist" is a person who owns or runs an industry/factory (उद्योगपति) — narrower; it stresses managing industry, not simply owning invested money.

• Option 2 "Minimalist" is one who prefers simplicity and the bare minimum in art or lifestyle (अतिसूक्ष्मतावादी).

• Option 4 "Leftist" is a supporter of left-wing, socialist politics (वामपंथी) — ideologically the opposite of a capitalist.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: entrepreneur (उद्यमी — one who sets up a business taking risks), investor, financier, philanthropist (परोपकारी), miser (कंजूस).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Ethically good behaviour one has
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Virtue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Virtue" means moral excellence; behaviour showing high moral standards, goodness of character. (सद्गुण / नैतिकता)

◦ One-word substitution: "Ethically good behaviour one has" = Virtue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Belief" is an acceptance that something is true (विश्वास) — it concerns opinion, not moral conduct.

• Option 2 "Virtual" is an adjective meaning "almost as described" or "existing on a computer" (आभासी) — cannot name a quality one "has" in this sense.

• Option 4 "Values" are the principles one considers important (मूल्य) — general and plural; the exact one word for good moral conduct is "virtue".

NOTE

• Word family: virtue (noun) – virtuous (adjective, नेक) – virtuously (adverb). Do not confuse with virtuoso (a highly skilled artist/musician).

• Antonym: vice (दुर्गुण/बुराई).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Contradict
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Contravene.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contradict" means to deny or oppose the truth of a statement; to say the opposite. (खंडन करना / विरोध करना)

• "Contravene" means to go against, to conflict with or to violate (a rule, statement or law). (उल्लंघन करना / विरुद्ध जाना) — the closest in meaning among the options.

◦ Example: The new evidence contravenes/contradicts his earlier claim.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Permit" means to allow (अनुमति देना) — unrelated.

• Option 3 "Verify" means to confirm the truth of something (सत्यापित करना) — an antonym-side word.

• Option 4 "Vouch" means to assert or guarantee that something is true (गारंटी देना) — also opposite in sense.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of contradict: refute, rebut, deny, gainsay, dispute, negate.

• Antonyms: confirm, corroborate, endorse, affirm, substantiate.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Graviety.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Gravity" — GRA + VI + TY, with no "e" before the -ty.

• "Gravity" means (i) the force that attracts bodies towards the centre of the earth, and (ii) seriousness or importance. (गुरुत्वाकर्षण / गंभीरता)

◦ Correct: They failed to grasp the gravity of the situation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sober" (गंभीर/संयत — serious, not drunk) is correctly spelt.

• Option 2 "Major" (प्रमुख — greater, more important) is correctly spelt.

• Option 4 "Pattern" (नमूना/प्रतिरूप — a regular design) is correctly spelt with double "t".

NOTE

• Beware of the "-iety" trap: variety, society, anxiety, propriety genuinely take -iety, but gravity, brevity, levity take only -ity.

• Word family: gravity – gravitate – gravitational – grave (serious).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

Unfortunately he is merely the head of a rabble of warlords who are (firmly) rooted in the past.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Stiffly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Firmly" here means solidly, rigidly, in a way that is not easily moved or changed. (दृढ़तापूर्वक / मजबूती से)

• "Stiffly" means rigidly, without bending or yielding (कठोरता से) — among the given options it is the only word conveying rigidity/inflexibility, so it best substitutes "firmly rooted".

◦ Correct: ... warlords who are stiffly rooted in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Feebly" means weakly (कमजोरी से) — the direct opposite of firmly.

• Option 2 "Languidly" means in a slow, listless, unenergetic manner (सुस्ती से) — opposite in spirit.

• Option 4 "Impotently" means powerlessly, helplessly (शक्तिहीनता से) — again the reverse of firmness.

NOTE

• Vocabulary from the sentence: "rabble" = a disorderly crowd/mob (भीड़/जनसमूह); "warlord" = a military leader controlling a region by force.

• Synonyms of firmly: securely, solidly, steadfastly, resolutely, rigidly.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. paneche.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "panache" — PAN + A + CHE (a French loan word).

• "Panache" means flamboyant confidence of style or manner; flair. (शान / ठाठ-बाट के साथ आत्मविश्वास)

◦ Correct: She answered the questions with great panache.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "palatial" (आलीशान — resembling a palace, spacious and splendid) is correctly spelt.

• Option 2 "scurvy" (स्कर्वी — a disease caused by deficiency of Vitamin C) is correctly spelt.

• Option 4 "oblique" (तिरछा — slanting; indirect) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• French-origin words with the "-che/-que" ending are a common SSC spelling area: panache, cliché, niche, technique, grotesque, picturesque.

• Static link: scurvy → Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency; rickets → Vitamin D; beriberi → Vitamin B1.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Abundant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Meagre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abundant" means existing in large quantity; plentiful. (प्रचुर / भरपूर)

• "Meagre" means very small in quantity; scanty, inadequate. (अल्प / अपर्याप्त) — the exact opposite.

◦ Antonym pair: abundant × meagre.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unconscious" means senseless or unaware (अचेत) — unrelated to quantity.

• Option 2 "Indefinite" means not clearly defined or limited (अनिश्चित) — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Unreliable" means not to be trusted (अविश्वसनीय) — unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of abundant: plentiful, copious, ample, profuse, bountiful.

• Other antonyms: scarce, sparse, scanty, insufficient, deficient. British spelling "meagre" / American "meager".

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I wished I (1) ______ teach this to Dhri as well, but I feared it was too (2) ______. Already he had started thinking like the men (3) ______ him, embracing the world of the court with open arms. And I? Each day I thought less and (4) ______ like the women around me. Each day I moved further from them (5) ______ a dusky solitude.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. could.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the verb "wished" (past tense), the structure expressing an unreal/unfulfilled wish takes a past modal. "I wished I could teach ..." conveys ability that the speaker did not actually have. (काश मैं सिखा पाती)

◦ Correct: I wished I could teach this to Dhri as well, but I feared it was too late.

• "Could" = past form of "can", used for ability in past/unreal contexts — exactly the sense required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "would" expresses willingness/habit, not ability; "I wished I would teach" is unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "can" is a present modal and clashes with the past verb "wished".

• Option 4 "may" expresses permission or possibility in the present and likewise cannot follow "wished".

NOTE

• Fixed patterns: "I wish I could ..." (present unreal), "I wish I had ..." (past regret), "If only I could ...".

• Modal pairs: can–could, will–would, may–might, shall–should.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I wished I (1) ______ teach this to Dhri as well, but I feared it was too (2) ______. Already he had started thinking like the men (3) ______ him, embracing the world of the court with open arms. And I? Each day I thought less and (4) ______ like the women around me. Each day I moved further from them (5) ______ a dusky solitude.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. late.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic expression required after "too" is "too late", meaning the right moment has already passed. (बहुत देर हो चुकी)

◦ Correct: ... but I feared it was too late. Already he had started thinking like the men around him ...

• The next sentence begins with "Already he had started thinking like the men ..." — this "already" confirms that the opportunity had been missed, so "too late" is the only logical fit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "early" gives the opposite sense and contradicts "Already ...".

• Option 2 "last minute" is a compound adjective used before a noun ("a last-minute change"), not after "too".

• Option 4 "later" is a comparative and cannot follow "too"; "too" is always followed by the positive degree.

NOTE

• Structure: too + adjective (positive degree) + to-infinitive — "too late to change", "too tired to walk".

• Do not confuse "late" (देर से) with "lately" (हाल ही में = recently).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I wished I (1) ______ teach this to Dhri as well, but I feared it was too (2) ______. Already he had started thinking like the men (3) ______ him, embracing the world of the court with open arms. And I? Each day I thought less and (4) ______ like the women around me. Each day I moved further from them (5) ______ a dusky solitude.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. around.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase needed is "the men around him", i.e. the men in his surroundings / in his company. "Around" is a preposition of place meaning on every side of, near. (आस-पास)

◦ Correct: Already he had started thinking like the men around him ...

• The parallel phrase later in the passage — "like the women around me" — is a direct internal clue that the same word is required here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "revolving" means moving in a circle around a centre — used for planets or doors, not for people surrounding someone.

• Option 2 "surmounting" means overcoming (a difficulty) or being placed on top of — wrong sense.

• Option 4 "rotating" means spinning on an axis — again a physical-motion word, unsuitable here.

NOTE

• Revolve = to move around another body (the earth revolves round the sun); rotate = to spin on its own axis (the earth rotates on its axis) — a distinction frequently tested.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I wished I (1) ______ teach this to Dhri as well, but I feared it was too (2) ______. Already he had started thinking like the men (3) ______ him, embracing the world of the court with open arms. And I? Each day I thought less and (4) ______ like the women around me. Each day I moved further from them (5) ______ a dusky solitude.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. less.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the repetition pattern "less and less", which means progressively decreasing. (उत्तरोत्तर कम)

◦ Correct: Each day I thought less and less like the women around me.

• The very next line, "Each day I moved further from them", confirms a steady movement away from the other women — so a decreasing expression is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more" would give "less and more", which is contradictory and unidiomatic.

• Option 2 "little" cannot follow "and" in this comparative pattern ("less and little" is wrong).

• Option 4 "limited" is an adjective describing a noun, not a comparative adverb of degree.

NOTE

• Comparative repetition patterns show gradual change: "more and more", "less and less", "better and better", "worse and worse".

• "Less" is used with uncountable/degree ideas; "fewer" with countable nouns (fewer books, less water).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

I wished I (1) ______ teach this to Dhri as well, but I feared it was too (2) ______. Already he had started thinking like the men (3) ______ him, embracing the world of the court with open arms. And I? Each day I thought less and (4) ______ like the women around me. Each day I moved further from them (5) ______ a dusky solitude.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. into.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Into" is a preposition showing movement towards the inside of something / entry into a state. (के भीतर / के अंदर)

◦ Correct: Each day I moved further from them into a dusky solitude.

• The verb "moved" indicates motion, and "a dusky solitude" is the state the speaker enters — exactly what "into" expresses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "on to" indicates movement to a surface (climb on to the roof) — unsuitable for an abstract state.

• Option 2 "up to" means as far as / as many as (up to ten people) — wrong sense.

• Option 3 "inner" is an adjective (inner peace) and cannot join "moved further from them" to a noun phrase.

NOTE

• In shows position (He is in the room); into shows movement/entry (He walked into the room).

• Vocabulary: "dusky" = dim, shadowy (धुंधला); "solitude" = the state of being alone (एकांत).

question: The National Literacy Mission (NLM) was set up in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1988.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Literacy Mission (NLM) was launched on 5 May 1988 by the Government of India under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.

• Its aim was to impart functional literacy to non-literates in the age group 15–35 years, the most productive section of the population.

• The mission was run by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (now the Ministry of Education) through the National Literacy Mission Authority (NLMA).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The NLM was later restructured as "Saakshar Bharat" (launched 8 September 2009, on International Literacy Day), with a special focus on female literacy.

• The current programme is "ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram" (New India Literacy Programme, 2022–2027).

• As per Census 2011, India's literacy rate was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%); Kerala was the most literate State and Bihar the least.

NOTE

• Article 45 of the Constitution (Directive Principles) originally called for free and compulsory education for children up to 14 years; the 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A making it a Fundamental Right.

question: The Constitution of India gives the right to vote to all its ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. adult citizens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution of India provides for Universal Adult Franchise under Article 326 — every citizen of India who is not less than 18 years of age and is not otherwise disqualified is entitled to be registered as a voter.

• Thus the right to vote is given to all adult citizens, irrespective of caste, religion, race, sex, literacy or property.

• Originally the voting age was 21 years; it was reduced to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (effective from 1989).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Non-citizens (foreigners) cannot vote in India, so Option 1 is wrong; there is no tax qualification (Option 2) and no restriction to males (Option 3).

• The right to vote is a legal/statutory right (under the Representation of the People Act, 1951), not a Fundamental Right.

• Elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India (Article 324), a constitutional body set up on 25 January 1950 — observed as National Voters' Day.

NOTE

• Related Articles: 325 – no person to be excluded from the electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex; 326 – elections to Lok Sabha and State Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage.

question: Which Sultan was defeated by Babur in the first battle of Panipat 1526?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ibrahim Lodi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The First Battle of Panipat was fought on 21 April 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty of Delhi.

• Ibrahim Lodi was defeated and killed in the battle; this victory laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India.

• Babur used the Tulughma (flanking) battle formation and the Araba device, along with field artillery/gunpowder, against Ibrahim Lodi's much larger but conventional army.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 Bahlul Lodi (1451–1489) founded the Lodi dynasty; Option 1 Sikandar Lodi (1489–1517) founded the city of Agra in 1504; Option 2 Mahmud Lodi was a son of Ibrahim Lodi who later fought Babur at the Battle of Ghaghra (1529).

• Babur was invited to India by Daulat Khan Lodi (Governor of Punjab) and Rana Sanga's rival factions; Babur wrote his memoirs, the Baburnama, in Turkish.

• Other battles of Babur: Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga, Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai, Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans.

NOTE

• Second Battle of Panipat (1556): Akbar/Bairam Khan defeated Hemu. Third Battle of Panipat (1761): Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas.

question: Which among the following minerals is essential for the synthesis of thyroid hormones (thyroxine)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Iodine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Iodine is the essential mineral required by the thyroid gland to synthesise the hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).

• The names themselves indicate the iodine content: T4 contains four iodine atoms and T3 contains three.

• Deficiency of iodine causes goitre (enlargement of the thyroid gland) and, in children, cretinism (stunted physical and mental growth). Hence the promotion of iodised salt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Iron (Option 1) is needed for haemoglobin; its deficiency causes anaemia.

• Selenium (Option 3) assists thyroid enzymes but is not the constituent element of thyroxine.

• Chromium (Option 4) helps in glucose metabolism (insulin action).

• The thyroid is the largest endocrine gland, located in the neck; it also secretes calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium.

NOTE

• Thyroid disorders: hypothyroidism (low T3/T4 — weight gain, fatigue; myxoedema in adults) and hyperthyroidism (excess — Graves' disease, weight loss, bulging eyes).

• Thyroid activity is controlled by TSH secreted by the pituitary gland.

question: Which of the following is an example of joint sector Industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Maruti Udyog Limited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A joint sector industry is one that is jointly owned and run by the government and private individuals/companies, sharing capital and management.

• Maruti Udyog Limited is the standard textbook example: it was formed as a joint venture between the Government of India and Suzuki Motor Corporation of Japan (1982 agreement).

• Such enterprises combine public accountability with private efficiency and technology.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• SAIL (Option 1) and HAL (Option 2) are public sector undertakings owned by the Government of India — SAIL is a Maharatna and HAL a Navratna company.

• AMUL (Anand Milk Union Limited, Option 4) is a cooperative sector enterprise — the Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation, founded in 1946, associated with Dr Verghese Kurien, the father of the White Revolution / Operation Flood.

• Classification of industries by ownership: private, public, joint and cooperative sectors.

NOTE

• Later, the government progressively divested its stake and the company became Maruti Suzuki India Limited, now a private-sector (Suzuki-controlled) company — but for the ownership-classification question it remains the classic joint-sector example.

question: The reign of Kumaragupta I the son and successor of ________ was one of peace and relative inactivity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Chandragupta II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kumaragupta I (reigned c. 415–455 CE) was the son and successor of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) of the Gupta dynasty.

• He assumed the title "Mahendraditya" and performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice; his long reign was largely peaceful.

• He is credited with founding the famous Nalanda Mahavihara (University) in Bihar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gupta succession: Sri Gupta → Ghatotkacha → Chandragupta I → Samudragupta → Chandragupta II → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta.

• Samudragupta (Option 4) is called the "Indian Napoleon" (by V. A. Smith); his achievements are recorded in the Allahabad Pillar (Prayag Prashasti) inscription by Harisena.

• Chandragupta II defeated the Shakas; the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign; Kalidasa is traditionally placed in his court.

• Skandagupta (Option 2), son of Kumaragupta I, repelled the Hunas and repaired the Sudarshana Lake in Saurashtra.

NOTE

• The Gupta age (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" — Aryabhata, Varahamihira, the Iron Pillar of Mehrauli, and the Ajanta paintings belong to this period.

question: Which Indian ministry introduced the Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 29 November 2021 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, then headed by Union Minister Narendra Singh Tomar.

• The Bill repealed the three farm laws of 2020 after year-long farmer protests; Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the decision on 19 November 2021 (Guru Nanak Jayanti).

• It received the President's assent on 1 December 2021.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The three repealed laws were:

◦ Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020

◦ Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020

◦ Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020

• Agriculture is a State subject (Entry 14 of the State List), while trade and commerce in foodstuffs falls under the Concurrent List — the basis of much of the debate.

NOTE

• Key agricultural schemes to remember: PM-KISAN (₹6,000 per year), PMFBY (crop insurance, 2016), e-NAM (2016), Soil Health Card (2015), MSP recommended by the CACP.

question: Which famous Indian dancer was the founder and director of the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts and received Padma Shri in 1965?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mrinalini Sarabhai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mrinalini Sarabhai (1918–2016) founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad in 1949 and served as its director.

• She was an exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, and was honoured with the Padma Shri in 1965 and the Padma Bhushan in 1992.

• She was the wife of the eminent scientist Dr Vikram Sarabhai (father of the Indian space programme); their daughter Mallika Sarabhai is also a noted dancer and activist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (Option 1) revived Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra in Chennai (1936).

• Prabhu Deva (Option 3) is a film choreographer, dancer and director from Tamil Nadu.

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (Option 4) was the legendary maestro of Kathak (Lucknow Gharana).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their States: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

question: Which is the governing body for Badminton in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Badminton Association of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Badminton Association of India (BAI) is the national governing body for the sport of badminton in India. It was founded in 1934 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

• It is affiliated to the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and conducts national championships and the selection of Indian teams.

• BAI also organises the India Open Super Series and runs the Premier Badminton League.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Famous Indian badminton players: Prakash Padukone (first Indian to win the All England Championship, 1980), Pullela Gopichand (All England, 2001), Saina Nehwal (Olympic bronze, 2012), P. V. Sindhu (Olympic silver 2016, bronze 2020; World Champion 2019), and the pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy–Chirag Shetty.

• India won the Thomas Cup for the first time in 2022 (Bangkok).

• Badminton terms: smash, drop shot, deuce, love, shuttlecock, let.

NOTE

• The other options are non-existent bodies. Other national federations: BCCI (cricket), AIFF (football), HI – Hockey India, AFI (athletics).

question: Which of the following is the instrument of monetary policy used by the RBI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Bank rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bank Rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends long-term funds to commercial banks without collateral. It is a classic quantitative instrument of monetary policy.

• By raising the bank rate the RBI makes borrowing costlier, which contracts credit and controls inflation; by lowering it, credit expands.

• The Bank Rate is aligned with the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Base rate (Option 1) is the minimum lending rate fixed by a commercial bank, not an RBI policy tool (now replaced by MCLR and the external benchmark system).

• The Call rate (Option 2) is the interest rate in the inter-bank call money market, determined by market demand and supply.

• Other RBI instruments: Repo rate, Reverse repo rate, CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio), SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio), Open Market Operations (OMO) and MSF.

NOTE

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and nationalised in 1949; its headquarters is in Mumbai.

• Monetary policy is decided by the six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), headed by the RBI Governor, with an inflation target of 4% (± 2%).

question: In which of the following regions, a cyclone is known as “Typhoon”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Japan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tropical cyclones are given different local names in different regions. In the North-West Pacific, i.e. around Japan, China and the Philippines, they are called "Typhoons".

• The same phenomenon is called a "Hurricane" in the Atlantic and East Pacific (USA, Caribbean), and simply a "Cyclone" in the Indian Ocean region.

• A tropical cyclone forms over warm ocean water (above about 27°C) and has a calm centre called the "eye".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Regional names: Willy-Willies – Australia; Baguio – Philippines; Taifu – Japan; Hurricane – USA/West Indies; Tornado – localised violent whirlwind of the USA.

• In India, cyclone names are decided by a panel of 13 countries under the WMO/ESCAP arrangement, coordinated by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), New Delhi — one of the six Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres.

• Cyclones rotate anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere because of the Coriolis force.

NOTE

• Recent cyclones in India: Amphan (2020), Nisarga (2020), Tauktae and Yaas (2021), Biparjoy (2023).

question: The Ganesh-rath is one of the finest monolithic temples located in________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mahabalipuram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ganesha Ratha is one of the celebrated monolithic rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) in Tamil Nadu, on the Coromandel Coast near Chennai.

• These monuments were built under the Pallava rulers, chiefly Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) in the 7th century CE.

• Mahabalipuram's "Pancha Rathas" (Draupadi, Arjuna, Bhima, Dharmaraja/Yudhishthira and Nakula-Sahadeva rathas) are each carved out of a single rock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984. It also includes the Shore Temple and the great open-air relief "Descent of the Ganga / Arjuna's Penance".

• Somnath (Option 1) in Gujarat is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas; Varanasi (Option 3) is the site of the Kashi Vishwanath temple; Nagpur (Option 4) has no such monolithic complex.

• Another famous monolithic marvel is the Kailasa Temple at Ellora (Rashtrakuta king Krishna I).

NOTE

• Pallava architecture stages: Mahendra style (cave temples) → Mamalla style (rathas) → Rajasimha style (structural temples such as the Shore Temple and Kailasanatha Temple, Kanchipuram) → Nandivarman style.

question: Which of the following is an example of micronutrient supplied by soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Iron.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Plant nutrients obtained from the soil are divided into macronutrients (needed in large quantities) and micronutrients (needed in very small quantities).

• Iron (Fe) is a micronutrient: it is required in trace amounts and is essential for the synthesis of chlorophyll and for enzymes of the electron-transport chain. Its deficiency causes chlorosis (yellowing) of young leaves.

• The micronutrients are: Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl (and Ni).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Potassium (K), Calcium (Ca) and Sulphur (S) — Options 1, 3 and 4 — are all macronutrients.

• The macronutrients supplied by soil are N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S; from air and water plants get C, H, O.

• N-P-K is the basis of chemical fertilisers: Urea supplies nitrogen, DAP phosphorus, and MOP potassium.

NOTE

• Deficiency symptoms often asked: N – general yellowing/stunted growth; P – purplish leaves; K – scorched leaf margins; Fe – interveinal chlorosis in new leaves; Mg – chlorosis in older leaves.

question: Who is the author of the tragic story, "Othello"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. William Shakespeare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Othello" (full title The Tragedy of Othello, the Moor of Venice, c. 1603–04) was written by the English dramatist William Shakespeare (1564–1616).

• It is one of Shakespeare's four great tragedies, along with Hamlet, King Lear and Macbeth.

• Its central characters are Othello, his wife Desdemona and the villain Iago; the play's theme is jealousy, called the "green-eyed monster".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• William Wordsworth (Option 2) was a Romantic poet — "Daffodils", "Tintern Abbey", and (with Coleridge) Lyrical Ballads (1798).

• Johannes Gutenberg (Option 3) was the German inventor of the movable-type printing press (c. 1440), not a writer of fiction.

• Charles Dickens (Option 4) was a Victorian novelist — Oliver Twist, A Tale of Two Cities, David Copperfield, Great Expectations.

NOTE

• Shakespeare is called the "Bard of Avon". Other works: comedies (A Midsummer Night's Dream, The Merchant of Venice, Twelfth Night), histories (Julius Caesar, Henry V) and 154 sonnets.

question: The festival of Holika Dahan marks the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. victory of good over evil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Holika Dahan (also called Chhoti Holi) is celebrated on the night before Holi, on the full-moon day (Purnima) of the month of Phalguna.

• It commemorates the legend of the demon king Hiranyakashipu, his sister Holika and the devotee-prince Prahlada: Holika, who was immune to fire, sat in the flames with Prahlada, but she was burnt while Prahlada was saved by his devotion to Lord Vishnu.

• Thus the bonfire symbolises the triumph of good over evil and the burning away of evil forces.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 refers to Durga Puja/Navratri, celebrating Goddess Durga's victory over the buffalo-demon Mahishasura.

• Option 4 (new year) applies to festivals such as Gudi Padwa, Ugadi, Baisakhi, Puthandu and Bihu.

• Holi is also called the "festival of colours"; regional forms include Lathmar Holi (Barsana), Hola Mohalla (Punjab), Shigmo (Goa), Dol Jatra/Basanta Utsav (West Bengal) and Yaosang (Manipur).

NOTE

• Vishnu's Narasimha avatar (man-lion) finally killed Hiranyakashipu — an episode narrated in the Bhagavata Purana.

question: India shares its boundary with which of the following countries in the east of West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bangladesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bangladesh lies to the east of West Bengal, and the two share a long international boundary.

• India–Bangladesh share the longest international border of India — about 4,096.7 km — touching five States: West Bengal (2,217 km), Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

• West Bengal also borders Nepal and Bhutan in the north and Sikkim, Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha within India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pakistan (Option 1) and Afghanistan (Option 4) lie to India's north-west; Afghanistan borders only Ladakh (PoK region) for about 106 km.

• China (Option 3) borders India in the north — the Line of Actual Control, about 3,488 km.

• Border lengths: Bangladesh 4,096.7 km > China 3,488 km > Pakistan 3,323 km > Nepal 1,751 km > Myanmar 1,643 km > Bhutan 699 km > Afghanistan 106 km.

NOTE

• Boundary lines: Radcliffe Line – India–Pakistan/Bangladesh; McMahon Line – India–China (Arunachal); Durand Line – Pakistan–Afghanistan.

• The Land Boundary Agreement (100th Constitutional Amendment, 2015) settled the exchange of enclaves with Bangladesh.

question: Badruddin Tyabji addressed the congress as president in _________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1887.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Badruddin Tyabji presided over the third session of the Indian National Congress, held at Madras (Chennai) in 1887.

• He was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress and a distinguished lawyer who later became a judge (and acting Chief Justice) of the Bombay High Court.

• In his presidential address he urged Muslims to join the national movement and rejected the idea that the Congress was a body of only one community.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 in Bombay at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College by A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant.

• Presidents of the early sessions: 1885 – W. C. Bonnerjee (Bombay), 1886 – Dadabhai Naoroji (Calcutta), 1887 – Badruddin Tyabji (Madras), 1888 – George Yule (Allahabad, first English president).

• Annie Besant became the first woman President (Calcutta, 1917); Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President (Kanpur, 1925).

NOTE

• Dadabhai Naoroji is called the "Grand Old Man of India"; he propounded the Drain of Wealth theory in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.

question: When the litmus solution is neither acidic nor basic, its colour is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. purple.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Litmus is a natural acid–base indicator obtained from lichens. In a neutral solution (neither acidic nor basic), litmus solution is purple (mauve/violet).

• In an acidic solution it turns red, and in a basic (alkaline) solution it turns blue.

◦ Memory aid: "Acid → Red; Base → Blue; Neutral → Purple."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other indicators and their colours:

◦ Methyl orange: red in acid, yellow in base.

◦ Phenolphthalein: colourless in acid, pink in base.

◦ Turmeric: yellow in acid, red in base.

• Olfactory indicators (onion, vanilla, clove) show a change in smell.

• The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: pH < 7 acidic, pH = 7 neutral, pH > 7 basic. It was introduced by S. P. L. Sørensen.

NOTE

• Common pH values: gastric juice ≈ 1.2–3, pure water = 7, blood ≈ 7.4, milk ≈ 6.6. Rain with pH below 5.6 is called acid rain.

question: With respect to sports, NADA stands for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. National Anti-Doping Agency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NADA — the National Anti-Doping Agency — is the national organisation responsible for promoting, coordinating and monitoring the anti-doping programme in sports in India.

• It was established on 24 November 2005 as a registered society under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, with its headquarters in New Delhi.

• Its work includes dope testing of athletes, results management, education and adoption of the WADA Code.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency) was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.

• India also has the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL), New Delhi, for sample analysis.

• The National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 gave NADA statutory status and set up a National Board for Anti-Doping in Sports.

NOTE

• "Doping" means the use of banned performance-enhancing substances or methods. Punishments may include suspension, cancellation of results and loss of medals.

question: Which ministry is related with “Deep Ocean Mission”?
option_2: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate change
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ministry of Earth Sciences.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Deep Ocean Mission is implemented by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). It was approved by the Union Cabinet in June 2021 with an outlay of about ₹4,077 crore for five years.

• Its objectives include the exploration of deep-sea minerals (polymetallic nodules), development of deep-sea technologies, ocean climate-change advisory services, deep-sea biodiversity conservation and an offshore desalination/ocean energy demonstration.

• Its flagship component is "Samudrayaan", which will send three persons in the submersible "MATSYA 6000" to a depth of 6,000 metres.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The mission is coordinated with institutions such as the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, NCPOR, Goa and INCOIS, Hyderabad — all under MoES.

• India has been allotted a site in the Central Indian Ocean Basin by the International Seabed Authority (ISA) for polymetallic nodule exploration.

• The Ministry of Earth Sciences also runs the IMD, the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting and India's Antarctic and Arctic research stations (Maitri, Bharati, Himadri).

NOTE

• "Blue Economy" refers to the sustainable use of ocean resources — the Deep Ocean Mission supports India's Blue Economy vision.

question: Ali Akbar Khan is associated with which of these instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Ali Akbar Khan (1922–2009) was one of the world's greatest Sarod maestros and a leading figure of the Maihar Gharana.

• He was the son and disciple of Ustad Allauddin Khan, and the brother-in-law of Pandit Ravi Shankar.

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (1989), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and was the first Indian musician to receive the MacArthur Fellowship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument with a deep, resonant tone. Other famous exponents: Amjad Ali Khan, Buddhadev Das Gupta.

• Option 1 Shehnai — Ustad Bismillah Khan (Bharat Ratna, 2001).

• Option 3 Tabla — Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha, Kishan Maharaj.

• Option 4 Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (string — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushira Vadya (wind — flute, shehnai), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam) and Ghana Vadya (solid — manjira, jaltarang).

question: What is the meeting point of the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Nilgiri Hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nilgiri Hills ("Blue Mountains") form the junction of the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats, at the meeting point of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.

• The highest peak of the Nilgiris is Doddabetta (2,637 m); Udhagamandalam (Ooty) is the well-known hill station here.

• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (1986) was India's first biosphere reserve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Palkonda Hills (Option 2) and Nallamala Hills (Option 4) are parts of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh.

• Cardamom Hills (Option 3, Elaimalai) lie in the southern Western Ghats in Kerala/Tamil Nadu.

• The highest peak of the Western Ghats is Anaimudi (2,695 m) in Kerala; that of the Eastern Ghats is Arma Konda / Jindhagada in Andhra Pradesh.

• The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap separates the Nilgiris from the Anaimalai Hills.

NOTE

• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012) and one of the world's eight hottest biodiversity hotspots; they are older and more continuous than the eroded, discontinuous Eastern Ghats.

question: Who has been appointed the Chairman of Staff Selection Commission (SSC) in February 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. S. Kishore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• S. Kishore, a senior IAS officer, was appointed Chairman of the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) in February 2022.

• The SSC Chairman is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC).

• He succeeded Bharat Bhushan Vyas in the post.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Staff Selection Commission was set up as the Subordinate Services Commission on 1 July 1976 and renamed SSC in 1977; it functions under the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, with headquarters in New Delhi.

• SSC recruits staff for Group B (non-gazetted) and Group C posts in Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, through examinations such as CGL, CHSL, MTS, JE, GD Constable, CPO and Stenographer.

• Vineet Joshi (Option 3) is known as a former Chairman of the CBSE and Director-General of the NTA.

NOTE

• Other recruitment bodies: UPSC (constitutional body, Article 315) for Group A civil services; RRB for railways; IBPS for public sector banks.

question: ______ poses are depicted on the gopurams of the Chidambaram temple (Tamil Nadu).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu has the 108 karanas (dance poses) of Bharatanatyam, as described in Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra, carved on the gopurams (gateway towers).

• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance, performing the Ananda Tandava in the "Chidambaram Rahasya" hall.

• Bharatanatyam, the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, is thus intimately linked to this temple's sculpture.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak (Option 2) belongs to Uttar Pradesh — gharanas of Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Kathakali (Option 3) and Mohiniyattam (Option 4) are the classical dances of Kerala.

• Bharatanatyam was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam; it was revived in the 20th century by Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer. Famous exponents: Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam.

NOTE

• Chidambaram is one of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams of Shiva, representing the element Akasha (sky/ether); the others are Kanchipuram (earth), Tiruvanaikaval (water), Tiruvannamalai (fire) and Kalahasti (air).

question: Which freedom fighter was also the first woman to become the Governor of Uttar Pradesh State?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sarojini Naidu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sarojini Naidu (1879–1949) became the Governor of the United Provinces (present-day Uttar Pradesh) in 1947 — the first woman Governor of an Indian State.

• She was also the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (Kanpur session, 1925); Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman President overall.

• Known as the "Nightingale of India" (Bharat Kokila), she was a poet whose works include The Golden Threshold, The Bird of Time and The Broken Wing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rajkumari Amrit Kaur (Option 1) was India's first Health Minister and the first woman Cabinet Minister; she was instrumental in founding AIIMS, New Delhi (1956).

• Rani Lakshmibai (Option 2) was the queen of Jhansi and a heroine of the Revolt of 1857.

• Kasturba Gandhi (Option 4) was the wife of Mahatma Gandhi and a participant in the freedom struggle.

• Sarojini Naidu's birthday, 13 February, is observed as National Women's Day in India.

NOTE

• Other "firsts": first woman Prime Minister – Indira Gandhi; first woman President – Pratibha Patil (2007); first woman Speaker of Lok Sabha – Meira Kumar; first woman IPS officer – Kiran Bedi.
